paperInfo.subject: Business Studies
paperInfo.paperName: Business Studies A-Level Paper 1 — Multiple Choice

questions.questionText: In Ansoff's Growth Matrix, what strategy is a Harare beverage manufacturer pursuing when it launches an entirely new energy drink targeted at existing retail supermarkets?

options.text: Product Development
Market Penetration
Market Development
Diversification

questions.explanation: Introducing a NEW product into an EXISTING market represents Product Development in Ansoff's Matrix.

questions.questionText: According to Frederick Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, which of the following acts purely as a Hygiene Factor rather than a Motivator?

options.text: Opportunity for achievement and promotion
Fair base salary, safe working conditions, and clear company supervision policies
Recognition for excellent performance
Job enrichment and greater responsibility

questions.explanation: Herzberg classifies pay, working conditions, status, and supervision as Hygiene factors (prevent dissatisfaction), whereas achievement, recognition, work itself, and responsibility are Motivators.

questions.questionText: In the Boston Consulting Group (BCG) Matrix, which product category generates strong positive cash surpluses from a high share of a slow-growing mature market?

options.text: Question Mark (Problem Child)
Star
Cash Cow
Dog

questions.explanation: Cash Cows hold high market share in low-growth mature markets, requiring little reinvestment while generating surplus cash to fund Stars and Question Marks.

questions.questionText: Which legal structure offers owners limited liability while prohibiting the sale of shares to the general public on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE)?

options.text: Sole Proprietorship
Public Limited Company (PLC)
General Partnership
Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd)

questions.explanation: A Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd) grants limited liability and separate legal personality but restricts share transfers and cannot list on the ZSE.

questions.questionText: Which feature best defines Elron Mayo's Human Relations Theory based on the Hawthorne Studies?

options.text: Worker productivity improves significantly when employees feel valued, consulted, and belong to cohesive informal work teams
Workers are motivated solely by piece-rate monetary wages
Strict bureaucratic rules and authoritarian supervision maximise output
Technology completely removes the need for workplace communication

questions.explanation: Mayo's Hawthorne experiments showed social cohesion, managerial attention, and group norms strongly lift productivity beyond physical conditions alone.

questions.questionText: When Price Elasticity of Demand (PED) for a firm's product is −2.5, how should the firm alter price to increase Total Sales Revenue?

options.text: Increase price sharply to raise margin per unit
Decrease price slightly, because percentage rise in quantity demanded will exceed percentage fall in price
Keep price constant because revenue cannot change
Stop advertising immediately

questions.explanation: |PED| = 2.5 > 1 means demand is price elastic: cutting price generates a proportionately larger increase in quantity sold, increasing total revenue.

questions.questionText: A smartphone brand launches a flagship model at $1,200 initially for early adopters before gradually lowering the price once competitors enter. Which pricing strategy is this?

options.text: Predatory Pricing
Penetration Pricing
Price Skimming
Loss-Leader Pricing

questions.explanation: Price skimming sets a high initial price to capture high consumer surplus from innovative early adopters and recoup R&D quickly.

questions.questionText: What is the main risk of operating a strict Just-In-Time (JIT) inventory system in Zimbabwe?

options.text: Inability to customise customer orders
Excessive warehouse rental and obsolescence expenses
Over-investment in buffer raw materials
Vulnerability to sudden transport disruptions, border delays, or supplier failure halting the entire production line

questions.explanation: Because JIT holds minimal buffer inventory, any disruption in delivery logistics or supplier reliability immediately halts operations.

questions.questionText: In Critical Path Analysis (CPA), what does "Total Float" on an activity represent?

options.text: The maximum time an activity can be delayed without delaying the overall project completion date
The shortest possible time to finish the entire project
A dummy arrow linking two parallel nodes
Capital tied up in raw material stock

questions.explanation: Total Float = LFT − Duration − EST. Critical activities have zero float; non-critical activities possess positive float.

questions.questionText: A business has Non-Current Liabilities $120,000, Issued Share Capital $180,000, and Reserves $100,000. Calculate its Gearing Ratio (Debt / Capital Employed).
Which motivational theorist introduced the distinction between Theory X (assuming employees dislike work) and Theory Y (assuming employees seek responsibility)?

options.text: Frederick Taylor
Abraham Maslow
Douglas McGregor
Victor Vroom

questions.explanation: Douglas McGregor formulated Theory X and Theory Y managerial assumptions in 1960.

questions.questionText: Under Porter's Five Forces model, when does "Buyer Bargaining Power" become strongest?

options.text: When raw materials are scarce worldwide
When the supplier sells a uniquely patented product with no substitutes
When industry barriers to entry are extremely high
When a few large retail buyers account for most of a supplier's sales and switching costs are low

questions.explanation: Buyer power is high when buyers are concentrated, buy standardised products, and face low switching costs.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly distinguishes Quality Assurance (QA) from traditional Quality Control (QC)?

options.text: QA builds quality into every stage of design and production to prevent defects; QC inspects finished goods to detect defects
QC prevents defects at the design stage while QA only inspects finished goods
QA relies strictly on random sample destruction at the factory gate
QC eliminates all supplier involvement

questions.explanation: QC is reactive inspection of output; QA focuses on systemic process prevention and Total Quality Management (TQM).

questions.questionText: How does a sudden depreciation of the domestic currency affect a Zimbabwean gold or tobacco exporter pricing in US dollars?

options.text: Exports immediately become more expensive for foreign buyers
Export competitiveness rises and local-currency revenue per USD earned increases, though imported fuel/machinery inputs cost more
Imported machinery automatically becomes cheaper
Domestic inflation drops immediately to zero

questions.explanation: Currency depreciation lowers foreign-currency export prices (or increases domestic-currency proceeds) while raising the local cost of imported inputs.

questions.questionText: In Kotter's 8-Step Change Model, what is the crucial first step leaders must take before implementing restructuring?

options.text: Distribute annual bonuses before announcing the change
Eliminate middle management layers immediately
Establish a sense of urgency so employees understand why change is necessary
Rewrite the Memorandum of Association

questions.explanation: Kotter's Step 1 is creating a compelling sense of urgency to overcome organisational complacency before building a guiding coalition.

questions.questionText: When a central bank raises interest rates sharply to curb inflation, what is the likely impact on highly geared businesses?

options.text: Lower dividend yield expectations
Cheaper bank overdrafts and booming mortgage demand
Automatic elimination of fixed overheads
Higher debt-servicing interest costs and reduced consumer credit spending, squeezing net profit margins

questions.explanation: Higher interest rates increase borrowing expenses for geared firms, discourage capital investment, and dampen consumer spending.

questions.questionText: What is the primary distinction between Horizontal Integration and Vertical Forward Integration?

options.text: Horizontal joins competitors at the same stage of production; Vertical Forward acquires a distributor or retailer closer to the final consumer
Horizontal acquires raw material mines; Vertical Forward merges with a bank
Horizontal diversifies into unrelated industries; Vertical Forward reduces capacity
Both always involve buying raw material suppliers

questions.explanation: Horizontal integration unites firms at the same supply-chain stage; vertical forward integration moves downstream toward customers.

questions.questionText: A company calculates Inventory Turnover as 8 times per year (45.6 days) compared with an industry average of 14 times. What does this signal?

options.text: Stock is selling out faster than all rivals
Stock is moving slowly, tying up working capital and risking obsolescence or storage costs
Gross profit margin is automatically above 50%
The business has excessive trade payables

questions.explanation: Lower inventory turnover means goods sit in warehouses longer, tying up cash and raising holding/spoilage risk.

questions.questionText: In Henri Fayol's Functions of Management alongside Henry Mintzberg's Roles, which Mintzberg category includes Monitor, Disseminator, and Spokesperson?

options.text: Decisional Roles
Interpersonal Roles
Informational Roles
Bureaucratic Roles

questions.explanation: Mintzberg groups managerial roles into Interpersonal (Figurehead, Leader, Liaison), Informational (Monitor, Disseminator, Spokesperson), and Decisional (Entrepreneur, Disturbance Handler, Resource Allocator, Negotiator).

questions.questionText: Which organisational structure delegates authority widely to junior managers across regional branches while reducing layers of hierarchy?

options.text: Matrix structure without team leaders
Tall, centralised bureaucratic structure
Autocratic sole-control structure
Flat, decentralised structure

questions.explanation: A flat structure has fewer management tiers (wider spans of control), and decentralisation empowers local branches to decide quickly.

questions.questionText: In Decision Tree analysis, a firm must choose Project A (60% chance of $200k payoff, 40% chance of $50k payoff; cost $90k). Calculate the Expected Monetary Value (EMV) and Net Gain.

options.text: EMV = $90,000; Net Gain = $0

questions.questionText: Which metric measures the proportion of a company's current profit paid out versus retained by examining Dividend per Share ÷ Market Price per Share?

options.text: Price/Earnings Ratio
Dividend Yield
Acid-Test Ratio
Capital Employed

questions.explanation: Dividend Yield = (Dividend per Share ÷ Market Share Price) × 100%, showing annual cash return percentage on the share price.

questions.questionText: Why does a business conduct "Test Marketing" before full national launch of a new food product?

options.text: To eliminate all fixed manufacturing overheads permanently
To obtain ISO 9001 factory safety accreditation
To gather real consumer sales feedback and refine pricing/packaging in a small representative region before committing full launch capital
To issue bonus shares to founding directors

questions.explanation: Test marketing trials the product in a limited geographic area to measure repeat purchase rates and fix flaws before costly nationwide distribution.

questions.questionText: What distinguishes "Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)" from minimum legal compliance?

options.text: Maximising short-term share price at the expense of pollution controls
Paying statutory PAYE and VAT taxes on time
Following minimum wage statutes only when inspected
Voluntary business initiatives beyond legal obligations to support community welfare, ethical sourcing, and environmental sustainability

questions.explanation: CSR goes beyond bare statutory duty, integrating social and environmental stewardship into business strategy.

questions.questionText: Under F.W. Taylor's Scientific Management approach, how are productivity gains achieved?

options.text: Time-and-motion work study to identify one optimal method paired with differential piece-rate financial incentives
Autonomous self-managed worker teams with job rotation
Eliminating performance targets completely
Replacing financial wages solely with social recognition

questions.explanation: Taylorism breaks jobs into standardised, scientifically measured tasks linked tightly to piece-rate pay.

questions.questionText: In Operations Management, when a factory produces 3,600 units against a maximum design capacity of 4,500 units, what is its Capacity Utilisation and how does this affect unit fixed cost?

options.text: 125% utilisation; unit fixed cost rises sharply
80% utilisation; higher output spreads fixed overhead over more units, lowering average total unit cost
80% utilisation; unit variable cost drops to zero
60% utilisation; total fixed cost increases linearly

questions.explanation: Capacity utilisation = (3,600 ÷ 4,500) × 100% = 80%. Raising utilisation spreads fixed costs across more units, reducing average cost per unit.

questions.questionText: Which element of a "Balanced Scorecard" evaluates internal operational bottlenecks, defect rates, and cycle times alongside financial profit?

options.text: Statutory Audit perspective
Balance Sheet Gearing perspective
Internal Business Processes perspective
Competitor Monopoly perspective

questions.explanation: Kaplan & Norton's Balanced Scorecard tracks four perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Business Processes, and Learning & Growth.

questions.questionText: Why might "Off-the-Job Training" be preferable to "On-the-Job Training" for introducing complex CAD engineering software?

options.text: It avoids any theoretical knowledge of software features
It guarantees zero travel or course fee costs
It immediately produces saleable factory output on day one
Learners receive specialist instruction free from workplace distractions and avoid costly mistakes on live customer orders

questions.explanation: Off-the-job training suits technical skills requiring specialist trainers and uninterrupted practice away from live production pressures.

questions.questionText: When a firm applies "PESTLE Analysis" prior to opening a branch in Bulawayo, which factors fall under the Legal and Technological dimensions?

options.text: Minimum wage/EMA environmental regulations (Legal) and mobile payment/solar power infrastructure (Technological)
Brand logo colour (Legal) and Maslow's hierarchy (Technological)
Internal cash budget (Legal) and staff absenteeism (Technological)
Gross profit margin (Legal) and balance sheet equity (Technological)

questions.explanation: PESTLE scans external Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental influences.

questions.questionText: What is the danger of "Overtrading" in a rapidly expanding SME?

options.text: Holding excessive surplus cash earning bank interest
Expanding sales rapidly without sufficient working capital, causing acute cash illiquidity despite rising paper profits
Having zero trade receivables on the balance sheet
Cutting sales below break-even deliberately

questions.explanation: Overtrading occurs when fast sales growth outpaces permanent capital, exhausting cash on stock/debtors until the firm cannot pay pressing creditors.
